specification.title: A unique violation is caught inside the transaction, which then ends normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `tx`, and make sure the write was sent to PostgreSQL.
Checkpoint `after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(), read through the transaction's own connection.

Insert the value 'taken' into uniq through the framework's ordinary write API. It fails with unique_violation (23505). Catch the error and continue. After catching the error, the callback sends nothing else and returns.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. The transaction is aborted, so it cannot run queries; the runner confirms the aborted state server-side.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework sends COMMIT.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When PostgreSQL has aborted the transaction before it ends, so that its COMMIT is answered with ROLLBACK, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: Connection::transaction(Closure) on one Capsule connection. Nested transaction() is a savepoint named transN. Eloquent creates write the markers. DatabaseTransactionsManager is not set. PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT is false. There is no pool.

configuration.transactions_manager: not set; Capsule does not install DatabaseTransactionsManager
configuration.pool: none; one connection on the Capsule manager
configuration.isolation: connection config isolation_level, applied by PostgresConnector when set; transaction() takes no isolation argument

execution.form: Managed Connection::transaction(Closure). Nested transaction() is a savepoint. Writes are Eloquent creates. The persistent mode is the same callback with PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction ends.
fault.preconditions: The row 'taken' already exists in uniq (fixture).
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction. PostgreSQL answers the later COMMIT with the command tag ROLLBACK, without an error, and commits nothing.
fault.expected_client: The driver receives the command tag ROLLBACK as the reply to COMMIT.

knowledge: The outcome reaches the client: PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT carries the command tag ROLLBACK.

api_outcome.basis: Connection::transaction() returned. When the callback returns, Laravel calls PDO::commit() if the transaction level is 1. The return value of PDO::commit() is not inspected.
api_outcome.contract: Laravel 13.38.0 Illuminate\Database\Connection::transaction() (ManagesTransactions) begins a transaction, runs the callback, and on return calls getPdo()->commit() when $this->transactions === 1. A thrown callback calls rollBack() and rethrows, unless the exception is a concurrency error and attempts remain. The default attempts value is 1. Connection::commit() calls getPdo()->commit() only when transactionLevel() === 1. A nested commit decrements the counter and does not send RELEASE SAVEPOINT. Connection::beginTransaction() at level 0 calls PDO::beginTransaction(). At level 1 or more it execs SAVEPOINT transN (Grammar::compileSavepoint). rollBack() to level 0 calls PDO::rollBack() when PDO::inTransaction() is true. A nested rollBack execs ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT transN (Grammar::compileSavepointRollBack). Neither commit() nor transaction() reads PDO::errorInfo() or a PostgreSQL command tag after commit(). executeBeginTransactionStatement() is getPdo()->beginTransaction() only. It takes no isolation argument. PostgresConnector::configureIsolationLevel runs "set session characteristics as transaction isolation level {$config['isolation_level']}" when the connection is opened, if that config key is set. This adapter does not set DatabaseTransactionsManager. Capsule does not set it either, so afterCommit() is not called on this path.

violation.message: SQLSTATE[23505]: Unique violation: 7 ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_code_key" DETAIL: Key (code)=(taken) already exists. (Connection: default, Host: 127.0.0.1, Port: 55435, Database: ppcs_tx_01a_caught_error_then_commit_mvibo9vw_b5b1d0, SQL: insert into "uniq" ("code") values (taken) returning "id")

session.query: select pg_current_xact_id()::text as xid, pg_backend_pid() as pid
select pg_current_xact_id()::text as xid, pg_backend_pid() as pid

evaluation.mechanism_detail: after the API returned, the session was "idle", and its last statement was "COMMIT"
evaluation.reason: TX-01A.1 violated: the API reported: committed

preconditions.description: the write of marker "tx" had reached PostgreSQL at `after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the duplicate insert failed with unique_violation (23505), as reported by the adapter
the top-level transaction was aborted before it ended: at `before-end` the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)" and pg_xact_status() already reported it aborted
PostgreSQL did not commit the transaction
